newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CEZ SHARES SURGE, SEEN UNDERVALUED.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CEZ SHARES SURGE, SEEN UNDERVALUED.

text.p: Shares in Czech power utility CEZ a.s. continued to rise strongly on Monday based on a growing perception, especially from abroad, that CEZ is significantly undervalued compared with other blue chip issues, dealers said.
CEZ rose eight crowns, 0.76 percent at Monday's fixing to 1,054 putting it nearly eight percent above its opening price of last Monday when 1997 trading on the Prague bourse began.

"CEZ has been very much lagging behind other blue chips...during the last three months but its very liquid and it has a positive profit outlook for the next few years," said Radim Bajgar of ING Barings.
"For me at the moment, CEZ seems to be one of the stocks that has good potential...I think that CEZ might definitley go to 1,100...by the end of the week or maybe even today," he added.
Last week CEZ crossed the 1,000 crown threshold for the first time since October 1996.
CEZ was harder hit than most blue chip issues during the downturn on the bourse which began in late Summer last year driven by fears about the poor regulatory framework of the bourse.
Investors have been put off from CEZ especially, dealers say, because of government ambiguity about deregulation of energy prices.
